title: Rapid escalation prep — Lena (NYC account)
content:
Purpose:
Fast prep notes for the emergency war-room with NYC Retail Co. They reported sustained elevated 5xxs and slowed streaming responses on hosted inference (api.redwood.ai) for their peak window. Goal: rapid triage, short-term mitigation, align owners, and produce the initial customer update within 30 minutes of session start.

Quick context summary:
- Customer: NYC Retail Co — production traffic hitting hosted-api in us-east1.
- Started seeing error spike at ~08:03 UTC; customer escalated via support@ at 08:15.
- Symptoms: intermittent 502/504 and streaming stalls after ~200 tokens; non-zero increase in token latency (P95 from 220ms -> 780ms).
- Impact: multiple user-facing checkout flows failing; estimated ~12% request failure rate during peak (customer metric).
- SLA: 99.9% request availability; they are on Dedicated Silver but routing to Hosted fallback in some regions per config.

Attendees and roles (draft):
- Lena Korhonen (me) — primary CS lead / customer comms
- Marcus Chen — eng oncall (serving-runtime), triage lead
- Priya Patel — SRE (infra/networking) oncall, scaling + infra
- Elena Ruiz — product (hosted-api) for feature/configs + rollout controls
- Optional: Diego (model ops) if model variant fallback needed
- Optional: Legal/PR standby if extended outage >2h

Agenda (30 min initial war-room):
1) 0-5min: quick situational recap + confirm ownership (who will talk to customer).
2) 5-12min: signal review (metrics, logs, traces) — Marcus/ Priya drive.
3) 12-18min: propose immediate mitigations (traffic routing, model fallback, rate limiting, cache flush).
4) 18-24min: assign actions with owners and ETA.
5) 24-30min: draft initial customer update and internal comms.

Immediate data to pull (priorities):
- Rolling 15min error rate across us-east1 endpoints (hosted-api) by model and route (Marcus).
- P50/P95/P99 token latency distribution by model/route (Marcus).
- Recent deploys / config changes in last 3 hours (Elena).
- Autoscaler events, GPU pool pressure (Priya).
- Router logs: Any elevated 429/queueing events (Priya).
- Customer-specific routing override history (Lena).

Hypotheses (fast):
- A: Recent kernel or runtime change increased tail latency for long sequences.
- B: Sudden traffic shift causing GPU saturation on a subset of nodes -> queue timeouts/stream stalls.
- C: Customer-side prompt pattern producing many long seqs or tool-calls causing KV blowup.
- D: Network/edge failure causing partial regional timeouts.

Short-term mitigations (candidate actions):
- Shift NYC customer traffic to alternate healthy region immediately (hosted fallback) — Elena to check region compatibility and cost implications.
- Enable model-variant fallback to a lower-latency quantized variant (if quality acceptable) — Diego/Marcus to validate.
- Apply temporary aggressive timeouts and retries at the router to reduce downstream queueing (Priya).
- Throttle non-essential routes (batch jobs, low-priority keys) for 15–60min window (Lena / customer config).
- Enable prefix/KV cache warm for recent session keys if applicable (Marcus).

Emergency runbook snippets (commands to run in war-room):
- kubectl get pods -n hosted-api -l pool=us-east1 — show GPU pod restarts
- gcloud compute instances list --filter=\"zone:(us-east1*)\" — confirm node availability
- curl -s \"https://metrics.internal/api/errors?service=hosted-api&since=15m&route=nyc\" | jq .
- redis-cli -h cache-primary.ft -a $CACHE_PASS INFO stats — check cache hit ratio
- routerctl reroute --source=us-east1 --dest=us-east2 --selector=customer:nyc-retail --drain-time=30s (verify with Elena)

Communication plan (first customer update — send within 30m):
- Short: Acknowledge, we are investigating, estimated ETA for next update: 30 minutes. No need to instruct customer to take action yet unless we ask them to temporarily reduce non-critical traffic.
- Medium: Confirm observed symptoms (availability %, time window), initial mitigations we started (region routing / throttles), expected next update time (30m), who to contact (Lena direct + escalation contact).
- Internal: Post summary in #cust-nyc-escalations, create/update Jira CS-2147 with current findings and assigned owners.

Draft first customer note (copy-paste base):
"Hi <Customer-PO>,
We’re actively investigating the increased errors and slow streaming you reported. Our on-call and operations are in a rapid-response session now. We’ve started collecting logs and metrics and will try a safe traffic re-route within the next 10–15 minutes to reduce impact. Next update from us in 30 minutes. — Lena, Redwood CS"

Action items (initial — owner — ETA):
- Pull per-route error metrics & traces (Marcus) — 10m
- Verify recent deploys & config deltas (Elena) — 8m
- Check GPU pool utilization & autoscaler events (Priya) — 10m
- Prepare fallback model variant readiness checklist (Diego / Marcus) — 20m
- Draft and send initial customer update (Lena) — 12m
- Post summary to slack and update Jira ticket CS-2147 (Lena) — 15m

Decision criteria (what forces escalation to full incident):
- >30% sustained error rate or >15m without measurable improvement after mitigations.
- Customer requests escalation to Execs or Legal involvement.
- Data exfiltration or security anomaly detected.

Notes to self / reminders:
- Keep messages concise and timestamped.
- Avoid promising timelines >60m unless we have a clear mitigation path.
- Capture all commands and outputs in the Jira ticket for postmortem.
- Save metric snapshots (png) from metrics dashboard right away.

Follow-up / post-war-room checklist (post-stabilization):
- Confirm full recovery and monitor for 2x normal peak window.
- Schedule a 60-min postmortem within 48 hours — include Eng runtime, SRE, CS, Product, Model Ops.
- Collect customer impact numbers for credits/SLAs (Lena + Finance liaison).
- Draft root-cause hypothesis list and action timeline; assign owners for permanent fixes.

Open questions to resolve during war-room:
- Any edge region networking events or cloud provider maintenance in last 2 hours?
- Are there any new model variants or kernel optimizations rolled in last 24h?
- Does the customer recent traffic pattern include longer sequences or new tool-calls?

Misc scratch notes (for war-room):
- If region re-route implemented, monitor for increased latency due to cross-region RTT — set alert if P95 > 800ms.
- Consider temporary token quota increase if rate-limiting causing retries.
- If model fallback lowers quality, offer customer a compensatory package and inform Sales for PSL.

End of prep notes.
